record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: A graph is AT-free if it has no asteroidal triple: there do not exist three mutually non-adjacent vertices such that each pair is joined by a path avoiding the neighborhood of the third vertex. What is the computational complexity of the Coloring problem on AT-free graphs, where Coloring asks whether a given graph has a proper coloring with at most k colors for an input integer k?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7 Determine the complexity of Coloring for AT-free graphs.
Note that graphs with asteroidal number at most 2 have no asteroidal triple. These graphs are also known as AT-free graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An asteroidal triple in a simple undirected graph G is a set of three pairwise non-adjacent vertices {u,v,w} such that for every pair among them there is a path in G connecting the two vertices that avoids the closed neighborhood of the third. A graph is called AT-free if it contains no asteroidal triple. The Coloring problem takes as input a graph G and a positive integer k, and asks whether G admits a proper k-coloring, i.e., a map c:V(G)→{1,…,k} with c(x)≠c(y) for every edge xy of G.

Determine the computational complexity of the Coloring problem when the input graph is restricted to be AT-free (with k part of the input). In particular, decide whether this problem is solvable in polynomial time or is NP-complete.
artifact.status_search_result: The complexity of Coloring on AT-free graphs is listed as an open problem in surveys on graph coloring for special graph classes. Partial results are known: Stacho showed 3-Coloring is polynomial-time solvable on AT-free graphs, and the problem is polynomial for fixed small k on certain subclasses, but the general complexity (with k part of the input, or even for fixed k≥4) appears to remain unresolved as of recent literature.

status_evidence.claim: The complexity of Coloring on AT-free graphs is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on the Computational Complexity of Coloring Graphs with Forbidden Subgraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of coloring complexity in restricted graph classes including AT-free graphs, with the general case left open.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys note the general complexity for AT-free graphs as not settled.
